answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when peers prove it is a duplicate. Like a falcon guarding a single nest, a comet leaving one verifiable trail, and a raven whose call is hard to fake, an identity must build costly signed history before it earns trust. Forging thousands of agents then means funding thousands of stakes and risking slashing, so the attack costs more than it can steal.
